status: Proposed concepts and validation plans, not implemented projects or measured outcomes
basis: 31 overall podium projects from 2017–2025; five supplementary 2025 category winners remain separate
selection: Conditional recommendations based on evidence traceability, bounded implementation and team fit; no statistical win ranking

ideas.name: FormTrail
ideas.summary: Guide a student through one complex campus form, linking every requirement to its source and showing exactly what remains incomplete.
ideas.user_problem: A student must reconcile instructions, attachments and required fields while completing a campus request. The proposed need should be checked with actual users before building.
ideas.workflow: Open supported form → see source-linked checklist → jump to a field → save draft → review missing items → export a review copy.
ideas.evidence: No Vote Left Behind connected an access problem to form processing; IntelliSchedule placed useful information inside an existing student task. A11y Tools, a supplementary category winner, adapted web interactions. Together they support a focused in-context workflow, not a claim that accessibility increases winning odds.
ideas.difference: The central feature is traceable completeness: distinguish a blank field, a missing attachment and an answer still needing review. Support one known form with manually mapped requirements; the product is not a universal form-filling agent.
ideas.mvp: One permission-compatible form or clearly labeled local fixture, keyboard-accessible checklist, field highlighting, local draft storage and export. Use ordinary browser DOM mapping and deterministic rules. Two people can own the interface and rules; a third can test accessibility and the pitch.
ideas.demo: Give a judge a deliberately incomplete form. Jump from two checklist items to the original instructions and fields; correct them; show the review state update and export. Do not submit to a real institution.
ideas.validation: Create ten seeded omissions and five valid examples; target all ten detected with zero false flags. Test the entire journey by keyboard. With five volunteers, counterbalance guided and original versions and report task time, omissions and the small sample size.
ideas.scope_cut: No automatic submission, eligibility decisions, universal website support or generated institutional requirements. Add language simplification only after the core works and retain the original instructions beside it.
ideas.dependency: A real, clearly documented form is the strongest input. If unavailable by hour 3, use a labeled fixture and describe user-need validation as pending.
ideas.conditional_fit: Consider an accessibility or student-experience prize only if its actual 2026 brief includes this use case. No current prize eligibility is established.

ideas.name: Contract Canary
ideas.summary: Show which user interaction breaks after an API response changes, with a replayable failing example and a visual explanation.
ideas.user_problem: A frontend developer sees a broken flow after a backend change but must connect the visible failure to the changed response field.
ideas.workflow: Load two API fixtures → replay one instrumented user flow → compare outcomes → identify changed fields → open a minimal failing interaction.
ideas.evidence: Freetear won first overall with a narrowly defined developer setup workflow. Pegasus, first in the virtual division, converted developer inputs into inspectable findings. The transferable pattern is removing a concrete development obstacle and making the result visible.
ideas.difference: Move beyond a raw JSON diff to a before-and-after application interaction. The prototype explains a failure in one instrumented flow; it does not promise to infer arbitrary application behavior.
ideas.mvp: A local checkout demo, two API versions, JSON fixture loader, explicit field-to-component mapping, replay runner and side-by-side trace. One teammate builds the runner, one the interface and a third the labeled examples. No cloud service is necessary.
ideas.demo: Rename an amount field or change its type. Show the checkout fail, open the response difference and replay the corrected contract. Also show an extra harmless field producing no break alert.
ideas.validation: Prepare twelve labeled mutations, balanced between breaking and harmless changes. Report the confusion matrix, false alarms and replay repeatability. Keep some mutations unseen until the demo rehearsal; do not report fixture performance as general compatibility accuracy.
ideas.scope_cut: One endpoint family and one application flow. Exclude production traffic, arbitrary authentication, automatic fixes and universal causal diagnosis.
ideas.dependency: A teammate comfortable with request handling and a small test harness. If interaction tracing is unfinished by hour 10, use explicit field dependencies and show that limitation.
ideas.conditional_fit: Potential developer-tool or technical-execution fit if such a 2026 brief exists. A sponsor integration should perform a necessary function, not merely host a logo.

ideas.name: Counterexample Arcade
ideas.summary: Teach binary search by letting learners break its rules, discover a small failing input and repair the mistake through animation.
ideas.user_problem: A beginner may recognize an algorithm's code without understanding why a boundary condition or loop invariant matters.
ideas.workflow: Change a predefined rule → search a bounded input set → animate a counterexample → explain the failure → repair the rule → replay.
ideas.evidence: AlgoSaurus made algorithms visible and won third in person; Chess 10 won overall with a changed-rule game. Tango connected practice with visual feedback. These precedents support an interactive learning loop with an observable consequence, not proof of learning effectiveness.
ideas.difference: The learner creates and fixes a failure. The distinctive demonstration is the smallest failing case within the tested bounds, rather than another animation of a correct sorting algorithm.
ideas.mvp: Binary search only, three editable rule choices, sorted arrays of length 0–6 over {0,1,2,3}, targets in {-1,0,1,2,3,4}, an iteration cap and animated pointers. Compare target presence with a reference implementation; any correct matching index is valid when values repeat.
ideas.demo: Ask the judge to change the loop boundary. Generate a small failing array, step through the missed target, repair the rule and rerun the same input successfully.
ideas.validation: Enumerate all 1,260 array/target pairs in this finite domain, ordered by length, array values and target. Verify counterexample minimality only within that ordering and domain. Ask five learners to explain the bug before and after; report observations without claiming a controlled learning study.
ideas.scope_cut: No arbitrary code execution, universal program verification, multiple programming languages or broad algorithm catalog. Describe bounded testing precisely.
ideas.dependency: Accurate algorithm logic and clear animation matter more than external APIs. If counterexample minimization is late, enumerate inputs in a documented size order.
ideas.conditional_fit: Potential education or interactive-experience fit if confirmed in 2026. Runtime AI adds little to the core proof; use it only for a separately evaluated feature.

ideas.name: WindowWise
ideas.summary: Find a feasible time for one campus errand between classes, accounting for office hours, walking time and required documents.
ideas.user_problem: A commuter must consult several sources to decide whether a short break is long enough to complete an errand.
ideas.workflow: Enter a class break and errand → check source-dated service rules → calculate a feasible visit → explain a conflict → revise the plan.
ideas.evidence: IntelliSchedule combined outside information for a student decision and won second overall. JAM organized scattered application information and received a third-place award. The reusable pattern is consolidation followed by a specific next action.
ideas.difference: Solve a constrained feasibility question: can this particular visit fit? A clear rejection with the conflicting time or missing document is part of the product, not an error screen.
ideas.mvp: Six service records, manually entered timetable, editable walking-time matrix, prerequisite checklist and source/verification date for each record. A browser app with deterministic interval checks is enough; no student-portal integration is required.
ideas.demo: Start with a feasible visit. Shorten the break, move the next class or mark a required document missing. Show the recommendation disappear and the exact constraint responsible.
ideas.validation: Use twenty hand-calculated cases covering exact closing times, travel buffers and prerequisites. Compare five users completing the same planning task against separate source pages; counterbalance order and report assumptions about walking and service time.
ideas.scope_cut: One campus and one errand at a time. Exclude live queue forecasts, institutional login, enrollment actions and dependent scraping.
ideas.dependency: Use manually verified public hours when possible. Label invented demonstration records as fixtures; do not imply that assumed service duration guarantees a completed visit.
ideas.conditional_fit: Potential student productivity or community brief fit if verified. The prototype can remain useful without adding an AI scheduler.

ideas.name: PantryRelay
ideas.summary: Reserve available pantry supplies for a pickup window and ensure that the last item cannot be promised to two people.
ideas.user_problem: A student may travel for supplies that are no longer available, while volunteers need a clear record of reserved, collected and released stock.
ideas.workflow: View available quantity → reserve a pickup window → hold inventory → scan once at collection → release an expired reservation.
ideas.evidence: DAOchow, second virtual, addressed shared community food resources. Pocket Park, second overall, connected available inventory with reservations. Their combination suggests an inspectable resource-to-handoff workflow; it does not establish demand at a particular pantry.
ideas.difference: Make reliable handoff the technical centerpiece: simultaneous claims, expiration and duplicate pickup handling. The scope avoids recreating DAO funding or a broad marketplace.
ideas.mvp: Twelve synthetic inventory items, two student sessions, one volunteer dashboard, transactional reservation logic and a single-use pickup token. Assign backend consistency, student UI, volunteer UI and testing across the team.
ideas.demo: Two browsers request the last item at the same time. Exactly one reservation succeeds. Collect it, repeat the scan and show that inventory does not decrement twice; then show a different reservation expire.
ideas.validation: Run at least twenty paired concurrent requests, ten expiry cases and ten repeated scans. Target zero overselling and duplicate collection in these tests. Ask a resource-desk volunteer to review the workflow if available; otherwise mark the operational assumptions as unvalidated.
ideas.scope_cut: One location; no payments, delivery, eligibility determinations or nutrition advice. Use demonstration inventory until a real operator authorizes integration.
ideas.dependency: The team needs someone able to implement transaction-safe inventory updates. If that is unfamiliar, select a simpler concept rather than presenting a race-prone reservation system as complete.
ideas.conditional_fit: Potential community or social-benefit fit under an actual 2026 brief. A blockchain or agent layer is not needed to demonstrate the core.

ideas.name: LostLink
ideas.summary: Match a lost-item description or photograph to a small found-item catalog, explaining candidate matches and allowing no match.
ideas.user_problem: Someone searching for a misplaced item must compare inconsistent descriptions and photographs across a found-item list.
ideas.workflow: Submit description or image → retrieve candidate items → show matching and conflicting attributes → shortlist for human review.
ideas.evidence: CloudPlate, third overall, connected camera recognition to a record and an action. EcoSort, a 2025 overall winner, connected an image to a practical next step. Transfer that input-to-record-to-action pattern. EcoSort is not evidence that runtime AI was implemented; its coding platform alone does not establish that.
ideas.difference: Focus on ambiguous matches and useful abstention: two similar bags should remain uncertain. Explain which visible attributes agree instead of asserting ownership from a model score.
ideas.mvp: A consented or staged catalog of thirty objects, one visual embedding or attribute-extraction component, text filters, candidate view and no-match state. Keep retrieval separate from custody or item release.
ideas.demo: Search for a distinctive bottle and inspect its candidates. Then show two similar black backpacks and an absent item; explain the uncertainty and abstention behavior.
ideas.validation: Create twenty alternate-photo queries, including at least five absent objects. Report top-three retrieval success for present items and false matches on absent items. Compare with a keyword/color baseline; keep evaluation images separate from catalog images and do not tune on the final test queries.
ideas.scope_cut: No ownership verification, facial recognition, campus-wide rollout or automated release of property. Text search is the honest fallback if visual retrieval adds no measured value.
ideas.dependency: Model access, latency and a useful image set are early gates. Check them by hour 3; unfamiliar model training is outside the 36-hour plan.
ideas.conditional_fit: Consider an actual vision or AI prize only if the model materially improves the measured retrieval task and its required technology is supported.

ideas.name: LineCheck
ideas.summary: Compare a purchase order with an invoice, highlighting quantity, price and total discrepancies with links to the source locations.
ideas.user_problem: A small organization must manually trace a mismatched total back to the exact document line and distinguish extraction errors from actual differences.
ideas.workflow: Upload two synthetic documents → extract supported fields → confirm uncertain text → reconcile line items → highlight each discrepancy in context.
ideas.evidence: AgentZero, a supplementary Capital One category winner, described invoice analysis. CloudPlate connected OCR with structured records. The transferable pattern is turning an unstructured document into an inspectable action; neither source establishes validated detection accuracy.
ideas.difference: Provide a verifiable source trail and arithmetic reconciliation. Show exactly why a line differs; do not claim to infer fraud or financial risk from a mismatch.
ideas.mvp: Two fixed document layouts, a preexisting OCR or document model, bounding-box references, a review screen and deterministic arithmetic. Support one currency and explicit line identifiers. Separate extraction, matching and presentation responsibilities.
ideas.demo: Upload an order and invoice with one changed quantity and one OCR ambiguity. Correct the ambiguous extraction; show that one alert clears while the real discrepancy remains tied to its source line.
ideas.validation: Use ten document pairs with twenty deliberately seeded discrepancies and clean controls. Report extraction errors separately from reconciliation precision and recall. Include at least one held-out layout variation within the declared supported family; disclose any unsupported cases.
ideas.scope_cut: No payments, tax interpretation, fraud labels, real customer documents or arbitrary accounting integrations. Use synthetic examples and a manual field-entry fallback.
ideas.dependency: Verify OCR access and bounding-box support by hour 3. If source locations cannot be retained, narrow the input to a supported format instead of inventing evidence links.
ideas.conditional_fit: Potential finance or document-AI fit only if the 2026 brief is compatible. The 2025 Capital One prize does not establish a 2026 prize.

ideas.name: Pulse Path
ideas.summary: Teach four tactile direction cues through a tabletop maze, then replay the player's route and mistakes on a companion screen.
ideas.user_problem: A learner needs a safe, repeatable way to practice decoding a small tactile command set and see how their responses compare with the intended route.
ideas.workflow: Choose route → feel a cue → press a direction button → record response → reveal path and errors → retry.
ideas.evidence: ARSL, second overall, combined learning with physical feedback. The Tilter, first in person, made a sensor-controller-output loop directly observable. The transfer is a tangible interaction whose inputs and results can be inspected immediately.
ideas.difference: A bounded tactile-language learning game replaces a broad navigation or recognition system. The companion replay makes the physical interaction explainable even to judges who cannot feel the device.
ideas.mvp: One microcontroller, available vibration hardware, four button inputs, four documented cue patterns and one maze. One teammate handles electronics, another the game and a third the replay interface. Use proper low-voltage motor-driving components already available to the team.
ideas.demo: Teach the four cues, let a judge try a short route, then reveal each cue and response on the screen. Repeat the same route and compare errors without claiming a validated learning effect.
ideas.validation: Bench-test fifty cue/response cycles for correct output and event logging. Record response latency, wrong turns and completion time for a few volunteers. Treat repeated-attempt improvements as exploratory observations.
ideas.scope_cut: No real-world navigation, autonomous movement, custom PCB or claims of accessibility effectiveness. A visual simulator is a separate fallback prototype and must be labeled as such.
ideas.dependency: Choose this only with hardware in hand and embedded experience. If a reliable cue cannot be demonstrated by hour 4, switch to the simulator or another concept.
ideas.conditional_fit: Potential hardware or learning brief fit if present in 2026. Historical hardware wins show precedent, not a hardware bonus.

ideas.name: StormTable
ideas.summary: Run a fictional neighborhood preparedness exercise in which stale reports and limited resources change the outcome of each decision.
ideas.user_problem: A student group wants to practice reasoning about incomplete reports and resource tradeoffs without treating an unvalidated prototype as a real emergency system.
ideas.workflow: Load fictional map → inspect timestamped reports → allocate a limited resource → reveal a scripted event → compare decisions and unmet requests.
ideas.evidence: HurriHome combined home status and a neighborhood view; Farsense connected remote sensors to a dashboard; FloodGuard, a 2025 overall winner, described a multi-source flood workflow. These precedents support making distributed information understandable. They do not validate disaster predictions or response outcomes.
ideas.difference: Teach information freshness and constrained decisions through a transparent simulation. Every outcome comes from visible rules and fictional inputs, rather than a claimed real-time forecast.
ideas.mvp: One fictional district, six locations, three scripted events, two resource types, timestamps and a deterministic rules engine. Build the state model first, then the map and debrief view. Browser graphics are sufficient.
ideas.demo: Give the judge two reports with different ages. Allocate a resource, reveal a changed condition and replay an alternative decision. Show how the declared simulation rules produced the different result.
ideas.validation: Test resource conservation, deterministic replay and expired-report handling across twelve scenarios. Ask five players to identify stale evidence and explain a tradeoff; report this as usability feedback, not real-world preparedness improvement.
ideas.scope_cut: No real alerts, evacuation routes, live hazard predictions, municipal integration or claims that a simulated optimum is safe in reality.
ideas.dependency: Keep the simulation's rules explicit and small. If the team cannot explain an outcome from the rules, remove that mechanic instead of generating a plausible explanation afterward.
ideas.conditional_fit: Potential education, community or simulation fit under a compatible 2026 brief. Agents are optional only where independent subtasks and their outputs are genuinely observable.

ideas.name: BranchBridge
ideas.summary: Give two players different evidence in a short mystery; their joint choices change the ending and a replay shows which decisions mattered.
ideas.user_problem: Players want meaningful cooperative choices rather than a linear story with cosmetic dialogue options.
ideas.workflow: Join two roles → inspect different clues → communicate → make a joint choice → reach an ending → inspect the decision trail.
ideas.evidence: Chess 10 won overall with altered game rules. Quests and Conflicts VR, a supplementary Netflix category winner, used branching interactive entertainment. Social Distance Beer Pong won second overall with an inspectable physical game interaction. These cases establish entertainment as a legitimate historical direction.
ideas.difference: Asymmetric evidence changes what each player knows, and the final replay proves that choices affected state. The core is cooperation and consequence, independent of VR or generated dialogue.
ideas.mvp: Two browser roles, one shared state machine, three consequential choices, two endings and reconnect support. Use a short authored script and simple art. Two teammates can split synchronization and the narrative/interface.
ideas.demo: Let judges take the two roles. Reveal that each has a different clue; record a joint choice; finish the short scene; then replay an alternative branch and show the changed ending.
ideas.validation: Enumerate every reachable branch and verify ending consistency. Test duplicate actions and reconnection during ten paired sessions. Ask players to explain which choice changed the outcome; report observed understanding rather than assumed engagement.
ideas.scope_cut: One short scene; no open world, generated story engine, headset requirement or large art pipeline. Keep the session short enough to demonstrate within the actual judging slot.
ideas.dependency: Synchronization must preserve one shared decision state. If networking is unreliable, a labeled local two-role mode can preserve the core mechanic.
ideas.conditional_fit: Potential interactive entertainment fit only if offered in 2026. Netflix's 2025 branching-narrative challenge is historical, not a current eligibility claim.
